text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless) I am probably one of the least intuitive people around when it comes to technology. I've bought quite a few gadgets that have ended up collecting dust as I never really learned to use them properly. My short lived relationship with a Palm Pilot ended in frustration when I didn't learn how to back it up on my PC and all my carefully inputted data was lost (more than once!) My kids use it now for a doodle pad. My husband says I have a "black thumb" when it comes to anything electronic. If there is a way to break it, lose it, or misuse it, I'm right there doing it. This is why it is so astonishing that I have grown to love my kindle 2.

I learned how to use it easily within a few minutes. It is so intuitive- my four year old enjoys it and can page back and forth reading classics such as George MacDonald's The Princess and The Goblin or Mary Pope Osborne's The Magic Treehouse. My tween age son uses it for Shakespeare- I downloaded the First Folio (35 plays from the Bard) for all of 99 cents! It's quite a favorite amongst my children and I have recently learned that if more than one family member has a kindle, all e-books may be shared with a single purchase. My friend can even access her kindle books and magazines from her iphone!

Cool features include 6 different options for font size, and text markers by "location" to bring you to the same line of text whether you use the biggest or smallest of fonts, as page numbers would vary too much to be useful. A male or female voice can read to you, though the voices are a bit stiff and robotic, and they make small mistakes such as using alternate pronunciation that don't fit context with heteronyms such as read/read or live/live. You can connect speakers or earbuds/headphones for this feature. Magazines can be downloaded as a single issue or a subscription, but the subscriptions cannot be canceled from the kindle- the user must go to amazon's "Manage my kindle" area to do this.

I have downloaded quite a few classic books for free and spent about a dollar on many others. So far, the younger children's literature has been somewhat limited, but I imagine that as prices drop, more will become available. I am a bibliophile and I never thought I would love a paper book replacement, but this device is so clean and glare free that I forget I am not looking at a paper page.

I'm sure that color kindles will be available within a few years, to make the illustrations a bit more interesting. I love the beautiful pen and ink type renderings which fill the kindle 2 screen when it isn't in use. Obviously though, color would be more attractive with other types of art. Black and white is easiest on the eyes for text, and mostly that it what kindle is all about.

The kindle 2 holds a charge for a long time. I think I plug mine in about once every couple of weeks. If you are not careful with the five way button, sometimes you do end up getting the wrong result. I purchased a book accidentally this way, but amazon has a handy "did you purchase this by mistake?" option which permits you to cancel the order if you act right away.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless)

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player It may not be a techie's delight, but if you are looking for a budget streaming device, this one fits the bill. First off it is quite small making it ideal for cramped or limited spaces like a vacation home or boat. It comes with a short, two foot long cable and a piece of two sided tape. It connects to your tv with the cable.Depending where you tv is located you might have to use a longer cable. I did and found that the tape is not just a nice idea, it is a necessity. the box is so small and most cables so rigid it flips the box off making it impossible to regulate with the infrared remote. Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express - HD Streaming Player

Bluetooth Speaker with LCD Display, NFC, FM Radio and Subwoofer Effect- Shower Speaker with Crystal Clear Sound and 3 Firm Suction Cups – Hands Free Speakerphone … (Red) [[VIDEOID:413906e1ac04fb2e066baa4adca5a20a]] This Bluetooth Shower Speaker with LCD Display by Abco Tech is the first shower speaker I've ever tried, so I can't compare it to any other one. I can share my impression of it from the perspective of one who hasn't used this sort of product before though and I hope that will be helpful to some of you who also haven't tried one before.

First of all, it measures 5 x 5 x 5 inches, and needs to be charged by USB after you receive it. Once it's charged you can attach it to a non-porous surface via three large suction cups in the rear of the speaker. We weren't able to get it to stick to our tile but it did attach firmly to the inside of the glass shower door and has held for three days so far without slipping or falling despite opening and closing the door.

The control buttons are easy to understand and operate. When you turn it on it makes a fairly loud beep, then the LCD display turns on and displays the time. I find having the clock very useful when trying to get kids out of the shower in time for school by the way! It has an integrated FM radio and you can preset up to 10 of your favorite stations and switch between them easily using the rewind and fast forward buttons. If you want to find different stations it will also do seek. When you select the radio mode it beeps loudly once again and then plays the station. Reception varies depending on signal strength, weather conditions and all the usual reasons. The default sound level is high but it's easy to adjust using the control buttons on the speaker.

Bluetooth: We had no problem pairing it to my daughter's iPhone 4S and streaming Pandora. In fact, the sound quality is excellent we thought! Once again the default sound level is high, but you can adjust that with the control buttons. ** It seemed as though we had problems getting it to switch to Bluetooth in the video, but that was because my daughter forgot to turn her phone back on for a moment. Once she did you can hear how good it sounded.** When you get a phone call while listening to the speaker it displays the calling phone number so you can decide whether to take the call or not, and if you decide to take it the speaker acts as a speakerphone.

Charge: So far it's been up for three days and we haven't had to charge it again, but then again we're only using it when in the shower or bathroom for longer periods of time so length of time it will hold the charge will vary depending on your usage. The rubber charging port cover doesn't want to stay covering the port up though, but it doesn't appear to have an effect on the speaker working.

We're very pleased by the quality, sound quality, and the features offered by this Bluetooth shower speaker so far. If anything changes I will update this review. I did receive a retail sample provided for evaluation and review consideration. I hope being able to see the actual speaker in position and working helps you to make a better informed buying decision. If you have any questions feel free to ask them in the comments section below and I'll try to respond as soon as I can. :)

Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.

text_fidelity_a:
Defender HD1T4 HD 1080p 4 Channel 1TB Security DVR with Mobile Viewing, Black We couldn't find a way to set this up because of logistics, which is unfortunate. Wireless or Bluetooth options would have worked better for this, not only because of distances, but because having to work with wires at such lengths and hide them in a home would have been beyond unwieldy.

Problem 1: drilling from the exterior of the house to the inside in Florida, unless done by a professional, likely means you created a place for water and moisture to leak in, which inevitably means mold and other issues. Even so, it's understandable that this may be necessary pretty much every time, and perhaps that wouldn't be such a big deal if it weren't for problem 2.

Problem 2: for this to work, you need to have a tv or monitor setup. If you have a bigger space, the distance might be further to get from where you want to record to the place where you have those things.

Here's what would have worked to let us set this up:
Have a hub of some sort that can be put anywhere nearish to the cameras, and then that can connect wirelessly to an app, computer, or monitor on the same network, not just for setup, but in general.

We would have had to go from the garage area to the inside part of the house, somewhere over 70 feet? To get to the nearest tv or monitor.

I'll try again for my small business if we ever change locations, but having to attach to a monitor is a pain. It should be able to work directly from the hub/DVR to an app.
text_fidelity_b: Defender HD1T4 HD 1080p 4 Channel 1TB Security DVR with Mobile Viewing, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR This review is for the Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR.

The pros:
-Light weight for a full-sized 60-inch tripod, especially for one made of aluminum.
-Unlike some other reviewers, I really like the carrying bag. The tripod fits just fine as long as the legs are telescoped fully, and the bag seems like it is well made. It has a zippered pocket on the inside with two spare hex keys.
-Pan function is very smooth. I don't shoot video often, but I can see that this feature will be very nice for those times when I do.
-Textured rubber feet grip well, and there are metal spikes which can be revealed if needed for extra grip on ice.
-Quick-release plate is metal instead of plastic. It also can be adjusted from side to side so that it can conform to a battery hatch on the bottom of a DSLR.

Cons:
-My biggest complaint is that there is no handle to maneuver the ball head. This makes it very difficult to make fine adjustments. A removable handle, or any sort of handle for that matter, would be a massive improvement for this tripod.
-The bubble level is on the body of the tripod. It should be on the ball head where it might actually be useful.
-The release locks on the legs are absurdly stiff to open. This makes it more difficult to extend them quickly, and also makes the tripod a very poor choice for anyone with arthritic hands. I believe it will also make it quite difficult to use in cold weather with cold, stiff fingers.
-The central column is very wobbly when fully extended, and the thumb screw used to stabilize it is totally insufficient for the task.
- Edited to add: after use in the field I found that the tripod maintains a certain amount of wobble for a few seconds after handling it, or in a breeze. It's not terribly sturdy compared to similar tripods.

Overall thoughts:
This tripod seems like a good compromise for weight and price. If I wanted a lighter tripod of higher quality I would have to spend a lot more money and get a carbon fiber tripod. I do regret the lack of a handle on the ball head. While it is not terribly sturdy, and I would not rely on this tripod extended to full height with heavy glass on the camera, for casual use it seems like it will work just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR

iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey Last year I switched to a Macbook Pro 13-inch after being a PC user since the early eighties. I love my Mac, but I haven't gone whole-hog for the rest of the pricey iProducts Apple puts out. Still, this case is just about perfect for my needs.

First, I like how the zippered compartment for the computer does not unzip all around. It's really easy to slip my Mac in and out of its fleecy padded pocket while still feeling like it's protected. (There's also plenty of room for my little wireless mouse dongle, although I don't use a mouse much anymore.) The iPad compartment is similar, and it holds my Kindle Fire in its rooCase with room to spare for something else (like a checkbook or wallet perhaps). The clever half-case compartment with pockets for chargers, headphones, and pens has plenty of room for my Mac power supply, Kindle charger and cables, and another charger if I need it.

The full compartment in the middle of the case is for whatever you might stick in it. It's not huge in depth, but it would certainly hold a legal pad/portfolio and a magazine or two. I don't use a cell phone now, but one day I might, so the outer pocket for the phone is nice; it's also serviceable for one of those small flashlights or perhaps a set of keys (on the right keychain). Toothbrush! I could see using the sleeve as a lapdesk/laptop stand while seated on a plane or in a doctor's office.

The sleeve comes with a classy, comfortable shoulder strap with strong, reliable clips. At first it wasn't clear what the the clips were supposed to clip to, but they are hidden away under the edges of the center gusset (what you see as the narrow black line running across the thickness in the photo here). There's no tangling up with this shoulder strap, either; the business ends can be rotated to keep the strap straight.

It's lightweight. And the color? It's a perfect match for the Mac Lion startup screen, of course. Everything about it says "Mac," including the iHome logo, but you don't have to be an Apple nut to love this sleeve. Very well designed.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Forerunner 910XT GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate Monitor - Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) As many have already written this watch has software issues. It does not display pace accurately. There's absolutely NO EXCUSE for Garmin releasing a training watch that doesn't know a person's pace. That's the sole reason this is getting a one star rating. On top of this, it is a simple software fix that they have still failed to make.

There is a simple work around: don't display pace and instead display lap pace. Lap pace has no issues and accurately describes your current pace. All the other pace features also work. Lap pace, ave pace, last lap pace are all accurate. The fact that everything else works fine shows to me it is just a software issue that Garmin could pretty easily fix if they bothered to spend 10 minutes on the issue. I probably would have given it four stars without this issue.

Why I really, really like this watch:

I bought this to supplement/replace my 405CX

The display is bigger and better. You can display four metrics at a time across four screens - so 16 metrics. The font is BOLD and easy to see even in tough conditions. While working out, you can hit the down or up arrow to more quickly get the screen you want to see. Also, even at its smallest, the font is bold and readable even to old eyes that don't see up close so well. The font describing each display is too small for my eyes to see when I have contacts in. So, I need to memorize which spot displays what. Still, this is sooo much better than the 405CX. On that watch, I can only see the big middle display with my contacts in.

The watch vibrates alerts. This is awesome!! I hate watches beeping at me and in loud conditions I would miss the beeps. I much prefer the vibration and I just turn off the audio alerts altogether. Also, the watch now alerts you (via beep or vibrate or both or none - your choice) when it has a GPS lock. The 405 never did this. Awesome improvement.

The battery lasts forever. Well probably not forever but you can use it for an entire day with GPS. The manual claims 22 hrs - I've yet to use it up when I started fully charged. The 405 claimed 8 hrs but it was really more like 6. Also, the 910 can be turned off so you can NOT waste the battery during travel time to your work out starting point.

It shows your recovery heart rate about one minute after you push 'stop' if you don't do the reset count downtime. Someone else mentioned that here. It a wonderful feature and not mentioned at all in the promotional material or users manual.

No touch bezel. The touch bezel in the 405 and 510 is a miserable feature. It has a life of its own in humid conditions which pretty much describes most of the heavily populated USA during most of the months of the year folks train a lot outside. The 910 completely relies on pushing buttons so now it only does things when you WANT the watch to do something. Also, the start/stop/lap/reset buttons are on the face of the watch. Everything else is on the sides. This keeps me from accidently hitting the wrong button when I don't mean to.

GPS programming seems smarter than the 405 / 510. With the 405 or 510 if you stop your movement and forget to hit stop on the watch it will keep adding distance. (For example, you can sit on a bench for a 15 minute break and it will add 0.5 miles to your distance.) I think this is because of GPS not knowing your exact location so it keeps seeing you as 10-20 feet from the last place it thought you were and keeps adding this up even though you are not moving. The 910 seems to do a lot less of this. It's still adds a bit of distance but over a 15 minute break it might be 0.05 miles instead of 0.5 miles.

Other things to note:

This watch is NOT smaller than other Garmin watches but it does stick out from your wrist less but to make up for that it is wider and taller. My guess is that it weighs pretty much the same. If you have a tiny wrist like mine, it can actually be a bit too big for your wrist. I got the cloth strap - this makes that issue much better.

I have not used it for swimming and I don't think I'm going to. It's not worth the risk if there is even a chance of screen fogging.

The manual not very useful. It doesn't show all the features. It is close to unintelligible. If I hadn't already had the 405 and was sorta familiar with how Garmin watches were organized, I'm not sure if I could have figured this out. Garmin's online help is no better.

Hint for female users: I skipped the heart rate monitor that came with the watch and instead got the original plastic hr monitor. I take off the strap and just place the main plastic part inside to top of my bra. It works great this way and is much more comfortable than having a strap wrapped around me and much easier to get in and out of and you don't have to find a private place to do it. I'm not sure if this will work for all women but it might be worth trying if you hate have a bra, HR monitor strap, plus shirt all binding around you like I do.

ETA 04-Jun-2012

I have found that lap pace isn't accurate either. Very disappointing. My latest work around is to reduce by lap distance to 0.25 miles. Last lap pace is accurate so by setting my laps as a very short distance, I'm getting constant feedback on my pace. Still, I think for a serious training regime, this wouldn't work. It's close enough for me.

(When I say not accurate, I mean not remotely accurate. It will show my pace as 10 minutes slower than I am going and it will stay that way for a full lap. Only when the lap is complete - it then shows total time for the lap correctly. It's not 5 minutes fast for half the time and 5 minutes slow for half the time. It's just off all the time and usually shows me as going at a pace 5-10 minutes slower than I am actually moving.)

On the a positive: another feature I'm really, really liking is the ability to manually scroll through the metric screens. I now set the screens to not scroll at all. I just use the up and down button and they get me to any screen I need. It's very nice for when all I care about is say, my heart rate. I just leave it on my HR screen but if I happen want to know my distance, then I can scroll to that screen and then back to my HR screen.

I'm also really, really still loving the giant display numbers. I can read these in any conditions. Rain, darkness, poor light, as I'm moving fast and don't have time to hold my hand still, etc.

ETA 09-Sep-2012
Garmin's support website has a post from 16-Aug-2012 that claims to have fixed the pace issue with a firmware update. I'm downloading it now. I'm planning an 11 mile hike today. I will post again if this fixes the issue.

See Garmin's site > tech support > search on 910 > search on 'pace issues.' Sorry, amazon removed the url.

BTW - I'm still using the 910 over the 405 despite the pace issue. The display and button functionality/placement of the 910 is just so superior to the 405 that it's worth the pace problems. I took my lap distance down to 0.10 miles so I get near continuous feedback on my pace that way.

Update 10-Sep-2012
The pace issue does seemed to be fixed!!! Or least, highly improved. The pace keeps nice and steady. It takes a few seconds of a changed pace for the watch to pick up on it which seems totally reasonable. Clearly there needs to be a lot of smoothing for the math equations seeing as GPS accuracy is only 15-20 feet and it only takes a reading every few seconds. Downloading the update is odd and I wasn't 100% sure it took but it does seem to have. My watch now displays my version as 2.6.

Upping my stars to five.

Update 07-July-2013.

With much trepidation, I just starting using this for open water swims. I've only done two so far in fresh water lakes. No fogging. Distances seem accurate enough. Maps show it has me within 30-40 meters of my real location. So far so good. I have not tried it in a pool.

I've also started using it on a bike. Just on my wrist. Lots of fun seeing how fast I'm going, etc but have yet to use it for any disciplined training. Just starting out but I really like it for this so far.

Also - Pace issue still seems fixed. It isn't as good as the old 405 but it also doesn't eat battery strength like the 405 did. I'll take the trade off.

Update 23-Dec-2014
I continue to heavily use this. Now the light has stopped working. It's past its warranty now. I'm reluctant to send it in to get fixed because I'm in training and don't want to be without it. It can be hard sometimes to get the charger attached these days. The attach points are extremely well worn at this point. I've used it 20+ time for swimming and have had no issues with fogging like some others have reported.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Forerunner 910XT GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate Monitor - Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

Ok, the downside to this..I read alot of books, mostly fantasy, that are in a series. Some of the series are in kindle form, and others in the series are in audiobook form only. This bites because altho it is nice to hear the book, you cannot follow along with it by reading it at the same time. If it had the words along with it, i wouldnt complain. Also, the audio book company that provides them offer you a "deal". I checked it out, it is not a real good deal at all. Mostly because you can get most audio books at a cheaper cost one at a time then you can with their deal. Alot of the books i want are about 8 dollars give or take, the Deal is for you to pay about 12 dollars each, but if you buy multiples, ie: buy 10 or 20 or 50 or 100 you get a small price break. The catch is that even if you pay a thousand bucks for 100 audio books, you can get them cheaper for alot of books one at a time. Unless that is, you do want a book that is over 12 dollars for the audio book. So, save your cash, get them one at a time and pay maybe an extra 20 cents but i see no real savings in paying alot of money now for a very small savings later, if at all. Back to the kindle. lighting is great, easy to use, lightweight even with the cover. I find however that i still try to physically turn a page before i realize all i have to do is click the button..lol I bet you will too for awhile...Have fun with this and happy reading..

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW), I own ALL of the kensington line of trackballs (clearly a trackball nut). From the original Expert Mouse (using a serial connection) all the way to this one. I can see how some purists are very touchy about their trackball performing and as it becomes an extension of interfacing with the computer, it's critical that it performs well.

PROS:
* Nice compact footprint; Not too demanding for space.
* Comes with the little ergonomic squishy thingy for a wrist-rest.
* The ball 'stays in' the unit even if you turn it over! This is a new concept for their trackballs! (you can pop it out if you need to condense for travel)
* Scroll wheel is nice; A feature present only in the higher-end trackballs.

CONS:
* BUTTONS! YUK! The button has some kind of contact issue where if you press it gently enough, you hear and feel a little 'click' but you didn't actuate the button! You must press it harder, and get a louder firmer CLICK! (really kinda mushy) to click it! I have tried different spots on the button and it's all the same! This is ALMOST a deal killer for me, but I'm going to give it some time, see if the button wears in and that false-click goes away over time.
* Scroll wheel is not free-flowing like on the modern expert mouse. With that sucker, you can fling the wheel and it will roll atleast for a half-second or so! This one really resists movement so it's more like a mouse-wheel than a scroll-wheel. It does not have a 'ribbed' feel, it rolls smoothly but it's not a 'on rails' as other models.

My personal favorite is still the modern expert mouse. It's massive (like a little tank on your desktop!) but you can navigate quickly with it, and use it in the manner a trackball was designed to be used.

Hope my review helps you!
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW),

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver) I am writing this review because after reading the few reviews available it sounded like this would be a great Media Player. But after receiving the player (a Christmas gift from my wife) I have to wonder if most of the people who reviewed the unit have actually used or even seen one in person. So I reread the reviews and noticed a trend that they don't actually say anything about using the player (all except one).
So here is a real user review.
The good. (I use it for music playback only)
The sound on the player is superb. I rip my cd's using the FLAC format and I have listed to playback using Wired (Grado's) and Bluetooth headphones. I have also listened to it on my home stereo using wired and a Bluetooth connection. There is a slight difference in the tonal quality but in a noisy environment my ears can't tell the difference. Sony digital processor does seem to color the music a little but it is on the warm side so it not objectionable.
I must say I love the sound of this player.
The media program (Media Go) that comes with it is very good for ripping music in any format that the player supports. Setting up playlist to send to the player is a breeze. The program does not have the options of JRiver Media Center but it is simpler to use.
The Bad
It is cheaply built - If feels like a toy. I do not believe it will stand up to daily use. Not a quality product that I have come to expect from Sony. For the price of this unit I expect it to at least have the build quality of my FiiO player or my cassette Walkman (which still works)
Bluetooth- It's a joke. My main reason of wanting this player was Bluetooth connectivity. If you disconnect it from the headphones, stereo -car and home, It take at least three tries for it to reconnect the next time you want to use it and you have to navigate to the Bluetooth screen to do it.
This creates a problem on its own. If you were listening to your playlist and stop at a particular track you now loose that place unless you navigate back to the home screen (more on that later) and bookmark your spot before you try and reconnect to your Bluetooth playback source. This is a major pain.
Screen Navigation. The player has 4 main buttons. The toggle button which surrounds the play and pause button is use for navigation. The navigation is more cumbersome -not user friendly- than it needs to be. Try and navigate while you are working out or somewhere not so well lit and it is frustrating at best. At this price it should have a touch screen. My 29 dollar SanDisk player is easier to use that this setup.
The next problem. You really can't power down the player. Once you power down the player if you accidently touch any button on the player it powers back up. I keep the player in a soft case clipped to my belt. I have bumped the player while in the case and have ended up with a dead battery the next time I wanted to use it.
There are other problems but they are minor and I can live with those.
If Sony wants to play in this market (no pun intended) these major flaws need to be fixed.
Tried to post a review on Sony's web site and they would not let it post. So I don't trust any reviews on their web site at this point. This is why I am posting it here to at least let potential buyers be aware of what it is really like to use this player.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)

Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Earbuds Sports Over-Ear Bluetooth 5.3 Ear Buds with Earhooks 120H Playtime Wireless Headphones for Workout Waterproof Audifonos Bluetooth inalambricos LED Power Display I find that the best price to performance is in the $30 range for Bluetooth headphones, and they keep getting better and better. I have several pairs that I use for the gym, general listening to music, watching movies, and playing poker. I like to have other charged ones ready to go if a pair gets low.

These were rated very well, so I decided to give them a shot. They are super comfortable and they stay in place at the gym. I am not an audiophile, but these are well balanced and have better sound quality than my other pairs.

The greatest thing about these is the battery life- I used them for about 11 hours, and there was still 50% battery life left. With all my other pairs the battery life is a real problem, and it does not improve as they age. The charging case is also nice and there is a display for remaining battery life of the case. Remaining battery life of the headphones is displayed on the mobile device.

The BT connection is also super reliable. I have not experienced any disconnects or interference.

There are a couple cons (no product is perfect) and I want to briefly discuss them.

1. The rubber snap-on ear buds are not universal. They have a unique oval shape where they snap on and are secured. I have a bunch of spares, but they will not fit on here. If you lose one or it breaks it is useless. It comes with 3 sizes, but most people are probably like me and can only use the one size that fits.

2. The gain is too high on these. Adjusting the volume from zero, there are not many steps until the volume is too high. This means that micro-adjustment of the volume is not possible. All my other pairs I can use at 100% volume or near this (though I would not recommend it) and there there are maybe 15 or more micro-adjustments all the way back down to zero. Also, the notifications "power on," "power off," and "connected" are too loud. It's possible that with different mobile phones they behave differently, and there may also be an adjustment for this.

In summary, I highly recommend these. They are comfortable, they stay in place, they stay connected to my device, and they sound great. Probably the biggest Pro is the battery life. I purchased these to use as a backup for my other pairs, but it turns out that these will be my main headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Earbuds Sports Over-Ear Bluetooth 5.3 Ear Buds with Earhooks 120H Playtime Wireless Headphones for Workout Waterproof Audifonos Bluetooth inalambricos LED Power Display

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W) This is an updated version of a mesh system router and satellite I already have. The technology is great when it's working, but, for whatever reason, my system has needed to be reset once a week or more, and the coverage is nowhere near as good as it claims it should be.

My hope was that the newer version would be faster and have better coverage. It isn't. It doesn't. And, like the earlier version, it has to be in AP mode to work with my FIOS modem (FIOS has a version of this available with its own firmware, but you have to buy a new one, and it won't work with any other ISP). Those hopes dashed, my next hope was that I could at least use the router as a satellite on my existing system, which, of course not.

So, you would think I could at LEAST use the satellite from the new one with the old system or the old satellite with the new one? They are the same model, after all. And that, too, would be a nope.

What I finally did, after hours on the internet (and other hours just trying to set up the new one by itself - it was the same with the old one - it for some reason despises custom settings and will not save them the first many times. It will also lose them after firmware upgrades, I expect, like its predecessor), was set it up alongside the old one with its own network name. Now I have one network serving one side of the house and the other serving the other. Speeds are good. So far, no routing issues, and I don't really expect any. The two network solution seems to have worked well for others.

But really.

If you are looking to expand your Orbi network, check out the nighthawk mesh expanders. I have the 7500, and it's excellent. Also, don't take my lukewarm review for a no-rec. The Orbi is, as far as I can tell from personal experience, buggy and locked down, but, again from personal experience, it beats the Velop (its nearest competitor) by a mile for coverage.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W)
